distinguishing_features: Continuous injection of a 0.5 mm SiC abrasive slurry during active brine reinjection
Silica-scale-specific detachment criterion based on particle-impact-enhanced wall shear stress
In-well mechanical scouring intended to prevent deposition rather than remove cured scale after shutdown
Downstream particle recovery via cyclones or conductivity-based particle monitoring
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent or remove adherent silica scale from geothermal reinjection wells without production shutdown while preserving injectivity and avoiding formation plugging or excessive equipment erosion.
parsed.viable_reason: The slurry cannot generally be recovered after entering the formation, so retained SiC would create severe plugging and injectivity risks, while the proposed 2 m/s operation also contradicts the stated SiC erosion limit of less than 1.5 m/s and relies on an unsupported scouring-stress heuristic.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: A skilled engineer familiar with mechanical scouring as an existing scale-control approach would readily recognize abrasive slurry injection as a routine implementation of that approach, with the claimed parameter changes not establishing a non-obvious mechanism.
